description: The three square wave tones and the noise generator of the Texas Instruments SN76489, the sound chip of the Sega Master System

params.text: Sets the pitch of that tone, two and a half octaves either side of C4
Sets what the noise runs at: fully anticlockwise it follows tone 3's frequency, and the three settings above that are fixed periods rising in pitch
Attenuates the voltage at that tone's MOD jack before it is added to the pitch, and inverts it below zero
Picks the noise flavour: one position gives white noise, the other the chip's periodic noise, which is pitched and buzzy
Sets the level of that voice, 0 to 15

inputs.text: Raises the pitch of that tone by a volt per octave; unpatched it reads the VOCT jack of the tone before it, and the first tone reads 0V
Moves the noise setting, each 2V raising it by one step, and does nothing until a cable is patched
Modulates the pitch of that tone, a full octave per 5V with the MOD knob wide open; unpatched it reads the MOD jack of the tone before it, and the first tone reads 5V
Flips the noise flavour set by the LFSR switch while it is above 2V
Scales that voice's AMP knob by the voltage here, 10V leaving the knob untouched and 0V silencing it; unpatched it reads the AMP jack of the voice before it, and the first tone reads 10V

outputs.text: Carries that voice's audio, hard clipped at 5V, with the audio of any earlier voice whose own output is unpatched added in

notes: the four outputs are chained: a voice whose output is left unpatched is summed into the next output along, so patching only NOISE gives a mix of all four
